attribution: Milequem Diarassouba — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Twin granite peaks of the Dent de Man rising above forested hills around Man
caption: The Dent de Man, the 881 m twin-peaked granite spire that watches over Man. It is the emblem of the Dan highlands in western Côte d'Ivoire and the centre of the trip's mountain section, reached by short walks from town.

commonsFile: File:Basilique notre Dame de la Paix de Yamoussoukro 9.jpg
alt: Dome and colonnade of the Basilica of Our Lady of Peace in Yamoussoukro
caption: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace in Yamoussoukro, consecrated in 1990 and modelled on St Peter's in Rome. A surreal midway stop between coast and highlands, and an unusual piece of 20th-century political architecture.

commonsFile: File:Le Musée N du costume de Grand-Bassam ancien palais des gouverneurs.jpg
alt: Colonial former governor's palace housing the National Costume Museum in Grand-Bassam
caption: The former governor's palace of Grand-Bassam, now the National Costume Museum. The historic quarter of this first colonial capital is UNESCO-listed and is the trip's opening day away from Abidjan.

commonsFile: File:Les chutes d'eau de la Cascade de Man dans la région du Tonkpi 02.jpg
caption: One of the waterfalls close to Man, a short walk or ride from town and a swimming spot after the highland hikes. Water levels are lower in the dry season, but the pools remain.

attribution: HAMIEN NGORAN YANICK — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Suspension bridge of woven lianas over a stream in the Dan highlands
caption: A woven liana suspension bridge of the kind built in the Dan villages around Man. Crossing one with a local guide is a core activity of the western section; condition and access should be confirmed with the guide beforehand.

attribution: Dadrik — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Dan mask held in a ceremony in Man
caption: A Dan mask in Man. The Dan masking tradition is still a living practice; ceremonies are seen through local guides and associations, with consent, rather than as staged shows.

attribution: Cyriac Gbogou — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Sunset over the lagoon and sandbar at Grand-Lahou
caption: Sunset at Grand-Lahou, where the Bandama river lagoon is separated from the Atlantic by a thin sand bar. It is the quiet, little-visited coastal stop at the end of the route, reached by lagoon pirogue.

attribution: Dadrik — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Palm-fringed beach and sand strip between lagoon and ocean at Assinie
caption: Assinie, a narrow strip of sand between the Ébrié lagoon and the Atlantic. Lagoon pirogue trips and quiet beaches make it an easy first or last night; sea currents are dangerous and swimming should stay cautious.

attribution: Nzunetu fotsing yves cedric — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
caption: Mont Tonkoui, at 1,189 m the highest summit around Man and a long but straightforward hike through classified forest. Early starts avoid the heat and the harmattan haze.

commonsFile: File:La vente au Marché de Bonoua en Côte d'Ivoire 01.jpg
attribution: Dadrik — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Vendors selling produce at the market in Bonoua
caption: A village market in Bonoua, in the south-east of the country. Markets like this are where the group eats: grilled fish, plantain, and attiéké bought from the people who made them.

attribution: Kod B — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Plate of attiéké, fermented cassava couscous, served with fish and vegetables
caption: Attiéké, the fermented cassava semolina served with grilled fish or chicken and tomato-onion relish. It is the staple of maquis (casual local restaurants), eaten in every town along the route.

commonsFile: File:Artisan tisserand de la ville de Man en Côte d'Ivoire 01.JPG
attribution: Neverdie225 — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Weaver working a narrow-strip loom in Man
caption: A weaver in Man working on a narrow-strip loom. Textile and wood-carving workshops in the highlands give a way to spend money directly with local craftspeople.
